correctness.rationale: For every integer n>=2, the uniform circular spacing vector is Dirichlet(1,...,1). Its simplex joint exceedance tails are (1-sum thresholds)_+^(n-1). Inclusion-exclusion plus layer-cake integration gives the stated finite covariance expression. Conditional on one spacing x, the remaining normalized maximum Z is independent of x, and g(x)=E max(x,(1-x)Z) is convex. The exact endpoint inequalities g(0)=H_(n-1)/(n-1)>H_n/n and g(1)=1>H_n/n, together with E g(X1)=H_n/n, imply one open interval of negative centered regression. The tail integral h(t)=Cov(M,N_t)/n has derivative -f(t)(g(t)-mu), is negative at the first sublevel endpoint, positive at the second and increases strictly between, giving a unique root and global strict sign classification. At t>=1/2, N_t=1_{M>t}; strict positivity at t=1/2 when n>=3 proves the location bound. Exact rational verification covered 2635 comparisons for n=2..18, and conditional regression quadrature covered 48 separate numerical checks. Computations are not substituted for proof. Boundary t=0 and t=1 are trivial zeros, excluded from interior uniqueness.

originality.rationale: The accepted claim is the universal one-sign-reversal theorem for covariance of the longest uniform circular spacing with the number exceeding a threshold, plus an explicit finite formula. Schlemm 2014 proves moments of the longest Dirichlet spacing and its Gumbel limit, but no mixed exceedance-count covariance classification. Holst 1980 obtains classical spacing order-statistic and exceedance fundamentals, from which the exact mixed moment is computable, but the inspected full text does not state the sample-size-uniform sign reversal. Hüsler 1982 and Holst-Hüsler 1984 study joint asymptotic circular coverage quantities; abstract evidence alone cannot exclude implicit finite implications, so inaccessible full-text priority remains a real risk. published-finding corpus semantic searches identified neighboring but non-dominating results concerning circular gap area and random integer compositions. A fixed-n first moment or marginal distribution does not imply the one-root cross-covariance sign law without a separate conditional-convexity argument.
residual_risks: Full text of Holst–Hüsler (1984), a particularly plausible historical joint-coverage article, could not be read. Its abstract alone cannot rule out an implicit stronger finite result.
The finite covariance formula is a classical Dirichlet simplex consequence; originality rests on the all-n strict unique-sign-transition theorem, not on the raw mixed moment.
Other early random-arc coverage literature may contain an equivalent finite conditional-convexity argument not located by the searches.

value.rationale: The longest circular gap controls whether equal-length arcs cover the circle, while the count of gaps longer than the arc length records how many uncovered holes remain. The universal exact one-crossing result identifies an unexpected negative-to-positive covariance transition between these two directly related geometric observables at EVERY finite sample size. This is a natural structural classification with a sharp uniqueness statement, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a mere restatement of a single known moment. n=2 has threshold exactly 1/2 and all n>=3 have thresholds strictly below 1/2. It gives a reusable geometric comparison fact independent of any downstream conjecture.
